must_fix: semiskill-review-by (line 14) is set to 2027-08-05, byte-identical to dv-sim-log-first-error's review-by date (also 2027-08-05, confirmed by reading that file's frontmatter) -- a direct violation of CLAUDE.md's explicit rule to 'STAGGER it, do not reuse a sibling's.' These two skills are the closest possible siblings here: dv-minimal-reproducer's 'When not to use this' names dv-sim-log-first-error directly, and step 8 deliberately copies its handoff field names verbatim. Pick a different date inside the 6-14 month window.

Dead handoff value: the primary handoff block's `class` field (step 8, line 250: 'class : design | infrastructure | unknown') is never assigned anywhere in the Procedure. No step in this skill says how to decide design vs infrastructure vs unknown -- contrast dv-sim-log-first-error, whose own step 3 does exactly this classification before producing the same field. Worse, step 6 of this very skill (line 215: 'the failure still appears with the block under test stubbed out or held in reset') generates exactly the evidence a design/infrastructure call should rest on, and the skill never wires that finding back to the field it promises to fill in. Two engineers will fill this differently -- one will silently carry forward the upstream triage's class, one will guess fresh from the shrink evidence, one will leave it blank. Add an explicit instruction, e.g. 'carry `class` forward from the original triage unless step 6 produced evidence to revise it, and say which.'

'Handoff template' slot (line 51: '[[FILL: what our bug ticket or handoff note requires as mandatory fields]]') is declared and never consumed anywhere -- confirmed by grep, its only occurrence in the whole file is its own table row. Step 8's two blocks are entirely fixed-format by design (explicitly copying dv-sim-log-first-error's field names, lines 242-243), so there's no place left for a team's own mandatory-ticket-fields fact to apply. Because the word 'handoff' itself appears dozens of times elsewhere in the file (it's what the whole skill produces), the pack's own mechanical check (consistency.py's C001, which treats a slot as 'used' if its label or just its first word appears anywhere after the table) will pass this file even though the specific fact is never spent -- a genuine false negative in the automated gate that this review is catching instead. Either wire it into step 8 ('append whatever additional fields the Handoff template slot requires') or delete the row.

'Config surface' slot (line 46) is likewise never invoked by name anywhere in the Procedure. Step 4's Configuration axis (lines 163-165) says what to switch off but never tells the reader to consult Config surface to find *where* those knobs live -- contrast the Hierarchy axis two bullets later, which explicitly says 'Use Glob on the paths named in the Testbench tiers slot' (line 170). This slot survives the same C001 substring check purely because 'config' appears elsewhere as a fragment of unrelated words ('Configuration,' 'config diff'), not because the located fact is actually spent. Wire it into the Configuration axis the same way Testbench tiers is wired into Hierarchy, or drop it.
technical_errors: Step 2's repeat instruction is silent on seed policy while the classification it feeds depends entirely on it. Line 111: 'Ask the engineer to repeat the unmodified test three times and to give you the path of each log' does not say whether the three repeats should pin the same seed or let it vary. But the resulting classes (lines 115-121) hinge exactly on that: 'Deterministic -- same seed, same signature, same simulated time of failure' vs 'Seed-dependent -- fails on one seed only.' Most regression harnesses auto-randomise the seed per invocation unless explicitly pinned, so a literal 'repeat the unmodified test three times' will usually produce three different seeds -- meaning the 'Deterministic' class (the one the table calls 'Ideal') can rarely be observed as instructed, and 'Seed-dependent' can't be properly probed either (that needs the same test tried against several *known, distinct* seeds, not whatever the harness happens to generate). The instruction should say explicitly whether to pin the seed for the three repeats, and separately ask for at least one deliberately different seed to test seed-dependence.

Minor: the axis cost-ordering claim (line 158, 'Each is cheaper to try and more likely to pay than the one after it') places Hierarchy (axis 4) ahead of Test length (axis 5), but axis 4's own text immediately concedes 'This axis often does not pay' (line 173) -- moving tiers usually means standing up a different testbench environment, which is rarely cheaper than trimming a warm-up phase of the same test. The ordering is defensible on risk grounds but the blanket 'cheaper ... more likely to pay' framing oversells axis 4 specifically.
verb_honesty: No hard violations found. Every simulation-affecting action is explicitly handed to the engineer: step 2 line 111 'Ask the engineer to repeat the unmodified test three times and to give you the path of each log', step 4 lines 177-178 'Propose exactly one change ... Then ask the engineer to make that one change, run it, and give you the path of the resulting log', step 4 line 161 'propose restoring close to the failure instead of starting cold'. The top-matter (lines 25-26) states the constraint plainly: 'it cannot start a simulation, build a model, or submit anything.'

Borderline readability issue, not a hard violation: step 4's five-axis menu (lines 160-174) is written in bare imperative voice with no per-bullet 'propose' framing -- line 160 'Cut the run so it stops shortly after the failure time', line 163 'Switch off what is not implicated', line 166 'Reduce the number of transactions, then constrain randomisation ... then replace the random sequence with a directed replay', line 169 'Move down a tier', line 174 'Trim warm-up, preceding phases, training or calibration sequences'. Read in isolation these look like agent-performed actions; they are only rescued by the step header ('Propose one shrink step...', line 156) and the handoff sentence that follows the list two paragraphs later (lines 177-178). Worth a light edit (prefix each bullet with 'Propose to...') even though the guardrail text technically covers it.
hallucination_risks: None found at high confidence. The domain-specific claims present -- UVM per-object seeding from an object's full hierarchical name (line 293), the determinism assumption that a fixed executable + fixed seed yields identical event schedule and X resolution (lines 127-129), and the listed nondeterminism sources (multi-core/partitioned sim, DPI/PLI + uninitialised C memory, co-simulation, wall-clock-derived timeouts, lines 132-138) -- are generic, verifiable UVM/simulation mechanics, not invented tool flags, message strings, or house conventions, and are pitched at the same specificity level the approved golden reference dv-ral-bringup uses for its own UVM internals (e.g. naming uvm_reg_mem_hdl_paths_seq). Nothing here needed a [[FILL:]] slot that is missing one.
budget_violations: Retrieval budget rule 3 (lines 79-85) claims completeness it doesn't have. It enumerates exactly three Grep groups that 'sit outside that per-iteration budget, and nothing else does.' Rule 4 (lines 86-87), immediately following, grants a further, unenumerated allowance: 'To locate a config knob or a tier directory, Grep for the knob name or Glob the tier path rather than reading the file -- then Read at most 40 lines either side of the hit.' This is not theoretical -- Procedure step 4's Hierarchy axis explicitly spends it: 'Use Glob on the paths named in the Testbench tiers slot and Grep for the failing component name to check it even exists at that tier' (lines 170-172). That Glob+Grep+Read (40-line windows, non-log files) is neither part of the per-iteration allowance (1 Grep fatal + 1 Grep pass + up to two 80-line log-Read windows) nor one of the three enumerated 'outside' groups, directly contradicting 'and nothing else does.' The budget section needs to either fold rule 4's usage into the accounted list or drop the false completeness claim.

'Pass marker' is priced into the per-iteration budget math (line 80: 'one Grep ... for the pass marker') but is never named by that label inside any numbered Procedure step. Step 1 (line 98) explicitly names 'the fatal markers from the slots table' but never the pass marker; step 2 (line 113) just says 'classify with one marker Grep per log,' not specifying that the check must include the pass marker to positively confirm a clean run rather than merely the absence of a fatal marker; step 5's 'No failure at all -> revert' branch (line 188) never says to confirm the pass marker actually fired. A reader following the numbered steps literally (rather than reverse-engineering the budget-accounting prose) could easily never check for it, and could then confuse a hung/truncated/infra-dead run with a genuine clean pass.
review.open_twice: Yes, on balance, once the must-fix items are addressed. The core reasoning is the real thing: the determinism-class taxonomy, the reasoned axis ordering, the sharp 'compare signatures not timestamps because axis 3/5 compress simulated time' insight (lines 203-209), and the Gotchas (checkpoint state, dump perturbation, UVM seed-by-name stability, shared-resource false negatives) read like genuine hard-won DV experience at the same caliber as the approved golden references, not filler. A DV engineer who used it once for a real shrink would likely return. But the identical review-by date shared with its closest sibling reads like this file was never actually reviewed, and a `class` field with no assignment instruction means the first real ticket this skill produces risks being mis-routed to the wrong owner -- exactly the kind of miss that costs a skill its second use. Fix the review-by collision and the `class`/Handoff-template/Config-surface gaps and it clears the bar comfortably.

recheck.why:
Lint is clean (`skills\dv-minimal-reproducer\SKILL.md [approve 1.000] clean`, 0 errors/0 advisories), the pack consistency checker returns zero findings for this slug, and metadata role/level are exactly dv-engineer/intermediate. The DV content is genuinely strong — the UVM random-stability point ("seeds each object's generator from its full hierarchical name, so adding or removing an unrelated component does not by itself perturb an existing component's stream") is correct and non-obvious, the nondeterminism-source list is right, "X differences between two runs are almost always a build difference" is right, the checkpoint-restore hazard is right, and step 5's four-way fatal/pass matrix is the best thing in the skill. Verb honesty is clean throughout: every action is Grep/Read/Glob or an explicit "ask the engineer... and give you the path".

But it does not survive question 2, and two of the failures are new this round.

(2) The budget does NOT account for every Grep. Rule 3 says "Four named groups sit outside that per-iteration budget, and nothing else does" and names steps 2, 3, 7 and 4. Step 1 is a fifth: it spends "**Grep** the log for the fatal markers from the slots table... then **Read** a window starting about 60 lines before it" on the *original* log, before any shrink iteration exists — and rule 3 assigns both per-iteration Grep calls to step 5 ("Step 5 spends both of those **Grep** calls every time"). Step 1's Grep and Read window are unpriced. The enumeration was tightened from three groups to four in this round and is still short by one.

(1/3) Steps 3 and 7 both instruct "**Grep** ... for the simulated time of failure". The time of failure is a value on a line, not a searchable string; no slot declares how it is printed (the End-of-run summary slot is a different line, the *total* simulated time); and no pattern is given. A literal agent must invent something like `@ [0-9]+`, which is exactly rule 5's ">200 hits, too broad" case. This breaks standing rule 4 (never Grep for something the engineer was never asked to define). It is also redundant: the failure time is on the fatal-marker line step 1 already Grepped and read into an 80-line window, and on the line step 5 already Grepped for the final log — so the budget spends two of its four carve-outs on calls that need not exist.

(5) `run id : <whatever identifies this run for us, from the run-identity slot>` has no step that assigns it. No step Greps a log for it, and unlike wall clock/tier/build status it is never listed among the things "can only come from the engineer". Worse, the slot table justifies duplicating this pack-wide row precisely by a narrowing — "Run identity here also asks where the string is printed, which the profile's entry does not" — and nothing in the procedure ever looks where it is printed, nor is such a Grep priced. This round then added a Human-verification check that depends on it: "the block says which seed is the reproducer's" — no field in either block is designated to carry the seed.

(5) The block's `phase : compile | elab | run | finalise | post` now contradicts step 1's new paragraph: "A `compile` or `elab` phase means you are in the wrong skill: there is no stimulus to bisect". `_shared/handoff-vocabulary.md` registers `phase` with narrowing `declared`; this skill structurally emits only `run | finalise | post` and declares nothing — no T2 row and no inline reason. C007 cannot see it because the block advertises the full set, which is the direction the checker does not police. This contradiction is new: the block already listed five tokens, the paragraph forbidding two was added this round.

(4) Nine of ten slots are spent. "Time-window controls" is not named by any step — axis 1 uses the fact but never cites the slot and, unlike axis 2 ("If that slot is unfilled, propose the change by description..."), gives no unfilled fallback. C001 passes only because the unrelated phrase "time-window shrinking becomes risky" appears at line 152.

(6) Yes — dv-engineer / intermediate, exactly.
(7) Confirmed 1.000 and clean.
(8) No. I would not hand this over today. Four of the items above are concrete enough that a reader following the text literally either cannot execute a step (the time-of-failure Grep) or fills a block field from nothing (`run id`, and the seed the verification section demands).
